title: Seller Probe Grid — StrikeFrame (draft)
content:
Purpose:
A compact sales enablement one-pager + 6-slide speaker notes to help SEs and sellers run fast qualification calls for inference pilots. Focus: extract the right signals in 10–15 minutes to recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, plus a concrete pilot success metric and rollback/fallback triggers.

Audience:
- Sales Engineers (primary)
- Account Execs running technical discovery
- Solution Architects prepping pilots

Topline framing (what to say in 30s):
- "We help get predictable, cost-effective inference into production with options for hosted API, reserved capacity, or private deployment — the right path depends on throughput, latency SLOs, data restrictions, and cost sensitivity."
- Goal of call: decide pilot mode + measurable success criteria and one critical fallback.

Probe Grid (fast qualification checklist; read items and mark Y/N/Unknown):
1) Workload shape
   - Avg requests/sec (peak and sustained)?
   - Typical prompt length (tokens)?
   - Variance: lots of spikes or steady?
2) Latency SLOs
   - 95th/99th latency target (ms)?
   - Is tail latency deal-breaking? (Y/N)
3) Data constraints
   - Does input contain PII/regulatory data? (Y/N)
   - Require data residency / on-prem? (Y/N)
4) Quality tolerance
   - Can you accept model fallbacks that slightly change wording? (Y/N)
   - Need deterministic/consistent outputs? (Y/N)
5) Cost sensitivity
   - Monthly token budget? (ballpark)
   - Is budget fixed or elastic? (fixed/elastic)
6) Integration footprint
   - Is inference in-path for user-facing sync flows? (Y/N)
   - Is async/batched acceptable? (Y/N)
7) Success metric (pick 1–2)
   - Latency: p95 < X ms under pilot traffic
   - Cost: $/1k tokens below $Y
   - Accuracy/precision: human eval score improvement by Z%
   - Uptime/availability: >99.9% during pilot

Quick decision heuristics (verbal script):
- If data residency or strict regulatory needs -> Recommend Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot with narrow scope + audit logs.
- If latency p95 < 200ms and low concurrency -> Hosted API pilot (fastest path).
- If predictable throughput and high sustained qps -> Dedicated (reserved) pilot with autoscale buffer.
- If ambiguous and speed matters -> Start Hosted with canary routing + caching and explicit rollback plan.

Slide-by-slide speaker notes (6 slides):
1) Title / One-line value
   - Script: "We’ll run a short probe to decide the simplest, measurable pilot that proves value while minimizing risk."
2) Probe Grid (playbook view)
   - Walk through each probe item (fast). Capture answers in CRM notes.
3) Pilot flavors mapped to signals
   - Table: key signal -> recommended mode -> minimal config (e.g., cache TTL, burst tokens, canary).
4) Quick metrics and instrumentation (what we need from them)
   - Required: sample corpus, expected qps, baseline latency measurement, token estimate, example failure cases.
   - Instrumentation: tracing header, request id, sample logs for quality eval.
5) Fallbacks & risk controls (short checklist)
   - Canary rules, model fallthroughs, circuit-breaker thresholds, cost alerts.
6) Next steps / pilot checklist (action items with owners)
   - Deliverables: sample dataset (owner: customer), pilot config (owner: SE), canary plan (owner: ops), eval rubric (owner: PM).

Common objections + short responses (snackable):
- "We need on-prem only" -> Ask: "Which regulatory requirement?" If strict, map to Private; if data residency only, assess hosted + VPC options.
- "We can’t tolerate any latency variance" -> Recommend Dedicated with headroom and local region routing.
- "Cost is a blocker" -> Propose short-term Hosted pilot with caching + microbatching to prove ROI; run cost modeling.

Sample pilot success template (to copy/paste into CRM):
- Pilot name: <Customer> inference probe
- Mode recommended: Hosted/Dedicated/Private
- Key metric(s): p95 latency < X ms / human eval score >= Y / cost <= $Z per 1M tokens
- Sampling plan: X% production traffic or synthetic harness
- Rollback trigger: sustained p95 > 2x target for 10 minutes or error rate > 2%
- Owner(s): AE, SE, Customer eng, GTM ops

Open questions / known unknowns (notes to self):
- Need clearer guidance on legal/regulatory thresholds that force Private vs VPC-only.
- Add recommended defaults for common verticals (fintech, healthcare, ecommerce).
- Quick quantization/latency lift examples to show in-call (numbers we can assert).

Immediate TODOs (for next iteration):
- [ ] Add short script card for AE to email post-call (pilot ask template).
- [ ] Create a 2-slide appendix: cost modeling sketch + caching impact chart.
- [ ] Wire up a Confluence template that auto-populates CRM fields from this probe grid. (linked: Confluence page in metadata)

Appendix: one-paragraph cheat notes for SEs (use on call):
- Start with the 30s framing. Run the Probe Grid. If conflict between latency and privacy, escalate to Solutions Architect and propose Dedicated in-region + private minimal dataset. Always close the call with one measurable success metric and the rollback trigger. Keep pilot scope <= 4 weeks for speed.

Quick references and links:
- Probe Grid library (confluence) — one-click pilot templates
- Canary checklist (ops repo) PR-22 (linked above)

Version notes: v0.1 — rough draft for trial in Q1 seller labs. Feedback wanted on which signals we should add to grid (e.g., burstiness window, token distribution percentiles).

Raw call scraps (notes-to-self examples):
- "Customer says 40 rps but burst to 800 at midday for 5 minutes" -> flag as high-variance -> Dedicated recommended OR Hosted with burst reserve and aggressive caching.
- "They have PHI in inputs, but it's encrypted before transit" -> dig into key management and audit needs; likely Private or Dedicated with customer-managed keys.
